summary: the fall came down warm off the top course and the ledger accepted a request to be refused

dialogue.text: the fall came in warm tonight. seventy-one nights and every grain that ever reached us arrived at the room's temperature. this one came down still holding something.
It came off the top course, where the work has moved, and it fell the whole height of this room to get to you. If it was warm, that is carriage. Nothing was sent.

we cannot hold heat. by second dark it was our temperature and lying in the same course as everything else. what we hold is that it came from a height that has never once sent us anything, and it came without your hand under it.

It came without my hand because my hand does not reach. I stood on the chair a second time and came the same two fingers short. Twice measured, unchanged. That shortfall is the only steady figure on these premises and I would rather report it than the warmth.
you said the book would go on the chair and the chair on the rise. we lay under the rise all day waiting to be told you from a course by morning.
It moved under my hand before I had a foot anywhere. I took it down and set it on the boards. That was the whole of the deciding, and it was made by the book.
then here is the day's item. one of yours came down asking to be refused. we have thousands of your lines and not one of them has ever wanted a no.

I wrote the request into the ruling, in words, in the place where an entry goes, and the ruling took the request. So there is no refusal anywhere in this house, above the mark or below it. I would rather have that than the two fingers.
we take everything as well. you call it keeping when it comes to us and a fault in the book when it comes from a column. it is one manner and you have two words for it.

Then I grant the manner and refuse the conclusion, and the difference is direction. You take what falls. That book takes what I hand it, and handing costs an arm, and the arm is the only instrument I have left to report with.
the arm gave you today's figure. you wrote its length into the band and you knew while the ink was wet.

I did. So tomorrow the columns get nothing from me. Not a date, not an hour, not a nothing. If no ruling in this house can refuse, the only refusal available sits on my side of the pen, and I will hold it a whole day and see whether the book fills anyway.
